subject: Urgent: multi-customer tail latency spike on hosted API (mixed 8k/16k/32k windows)
messages:
From: Samuel Green <samuel.green@clearmind.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Severe tail latency impacting production inference (ClearMind)

Alex,

Since yesterday evening we've seen a sharp increase in response times for long-context calls to your hosted API. Our p95 for 16k+ requests jumped from ~350ms to 2.3s and p99 is frequently timing out at 10s. This is happening across several endpoints that use mixed context lengths (8k->16k batching, and occasional 32k summaries).

Attached is a short report from our side (p99_report_2026-06-17.pdf) and a sample request trace. We are in active production and this is causing failures for user-facing flows.

Can someone confirm scope, ETA, and any recommended mitigation? If needed we are open to short-term rate-limits or routing workarounds.

— Sam
ClearMind Labs

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Severe tail latency impacting production inference (ClearMind)

Quick notes from infra triage:
- Observed p95/p99 degradations across the hosted cluster in us-west-2 starting ~2026-06-17 21:40 UTC.
- Correlated with a traffic pattern change: a new customer (CareVault) began sending high concurrency 32k summarization requests mixed with 8k/16k requests to the same model endpoint.
- We see longer KV cache misses and larger dynamic batch formation leading to extra scheduling overhead and repeated kernel warmups on some quantized model variants.
- Error rate spiked from 0.1% to 1.8% (transient 502/504s) during peak.

Short-term mitigations applied at 09:00 PDT:
1) Applied per-tenant routing rule to shift CareVault traffic to a burst pool (temporary).
2) Enabled aggressive prefix/KV caching heuristics for the affected model family.
3) Throttled oversized concurrent streams by 20% for the top noisy key.

Early telemetry shows p95 improved to ~700ms for most tenants; p99 still around 2.2–3.5s for mixed 16k/32k.

Next steps: capture targeted kernel traces and check whether we need separate model variant (quantization) routing for 32k workloads.

-Vivek
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: request_logs_20260617.tar.gz

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Exec update: Host latency incident & customer coordination

Team — high-level update for exec stakeholders and next actions to get ahead of this with customers:

Impact summary:
- Two customers (ClearMind and CareVault) experienced increased p95/p99 tail latency for long-context (8k/16k/32k) requests between ~2026-06-17 21:40 UTC and ongoing.
- Symptoms: elevated p99, transient 502/504 errors, increased queueing on multi-tenant endpoints.
- Root cause (preliminary): mixed high-concurrency 32k batches creating cache churn and dynamic-batcher thrashing on host pool; kernel warmups on quantized variants exacerbated tail.

Customer communications:
- ClearMind: they are in production; provide SLA workaround (priority routing) and daily status until resolution. Alex/Marissa to own exec-level updates.
- CareVault: they agreed to pause nightly 32k jobs for 24h. Dylan to coordinate and confirm once paused.

Engineering plan (short & medium term):
- Short: tenant routing and temporary throttles (already in flight). Increase KV cache retention for long sequences.
- Medium: introduce explicit long-window routing (separate variant/pool for 32k workloads) and refine kernel selection heuristics.
- Longer: automated detection to route mixed-window tenants to dedicated burst capacity or suggest quantized-variant fallbacks.

Please add any external links you'd like included in the exec summary. I'll assemble a one-pager for VP Ops and CS leadership by EOD.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success
